correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and southeastward inland-ice corridor
correspondence.finding: The chosen headward opening and entire initial southeastward corridor are within the national original’s southern Inland Ice area. The original graticule, ice contours and distinction from the exposed coastal rock belt locate this interval. No river trace or hydronym is established by the ice-surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours or aeromagnetic lineaments.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern ice-field bend and southwestward nunatak/ice-margin passage
correspondence.finding: The selected westward bend and subsequent southwestward passage are fully within the original’s ice field and scattered exposed-rock/nunatak setting. The selected smaller turns and intervening intervals are included in the comparison. Ice and rock exposures are geographic terrain evidence; they do not establish a connected surface or subglacial river.

correspondence.component_scope: Western turn into the exposed-rock and valley belt
correspondence.finding: The western and southwestward selected intervals enter the irregular boundary between ice, outlying rock exposures and the continuous exposed-rock belt east of the source-labelled Narsarsuaq area. The complete intermediate bends and passages among mapped rock masses are geographically accounted for. No through-valley river name, lake name or glacier name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southward passage and approach to the fragment junction
correspondence.finding: After the western turn, the selected path runs southward through the mapped rock-and-valley/ice-margin terrain. This includes the long final southward part of FID8925 and its exact stored end, rather than stopping the review at the first exposed-rock area. The thematic map supplies complete regional terrain coverage but does not survey the selected route as a natural river.

correspondence.component_scope: FID8925–8926 junction and complete final fragment
correspondence.finding: The junction is inside the same continuous original-map coverage. All of FID8926 is included: its first southward passage, short reversing bends, westward turn and final southwestward ending. The selected terminal lies in the map’s inland exposed-rock and narrow valley setting southeast of Narsarsuaq; the source does not independently establish this stored ending as an ordinary river mouth or a present-day ice front.

correspondence.component_scope: 61512470-chosen-opening
correspondence.finding: The selected western opening lies just southeast of Melo and initially trends east before turning southeast near the southern margin of the La Picasa study-area depiction. The original research map separates it from reservoir R1 and the managed drainage corridor farther north. Neither the study figure nor the generalized Córdoba sheet establishes a named opening channel.

correspondence.component_scope: 61512470-southeastern-cross-border-continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected line continues southeast into northern Buenos Aires, away from the regulation-lagoon chain depicted in the La Picasa research. The regional figures establish that separation, but do not map a continuous corresponding watercourse through this long selected interval.

correspondence.component_scope: 61512470-southern-western-eastward-links
correspondence.finding: After the major southeastward descent, the selected line turns generally east through lowland country well south of the mapped La Picasa internal canal system. This portion is largely outside the study figure’s useful hydrographic coverage. The province-scale Córdoba sheet does not provide the missing northern Buenos Aires detail.

correspondence.component_scope: 61512470-southern-central-bends
correspondence.finding: The selected southern corridor makes several northeastward and southeastward bends before resuming an eastward direction. No inspected independent original establishes these intermediate joins as one connected natural channel or as a particular named canal. The documented La Picasa diversion works farther north are not substituted for the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: 61512470-lower-eastward-approach
correspondence.finding: The selected line has a further sustained eastward reach south of the La Picasa lake setting. The source map places the named receiving lake and its works to the north, without supplying corresponding hydrographic detail along this selected approach.

correspondence.component_scope: 61512470-actual-terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual selected ending turns south and then slightly southwest, well south of the mapped Laguna La Picasa and outside the research figure’s detailed terminal coverage. It is not the lake endpoint established for the separate earlier selection. No inspected source identifies this endpoint as a named stream junction, lake, canal or natural mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and upper eastward trunk
correspondence.finding: The western headward channel near Cerro Deri runs north, then northeast and east into the labelled Telire trunk. Turi labels a separate side branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Telire, principal confluence and northward turn
correspondence.finding: The eastward Telire approach joins the Yorkín receiving corridor and turns north into Sixaola. An exact name-change vertex is not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: First simplified eastward border reach
correspondence.finding: The straightened selection corresponds to the connected eastward Sixaola valley; source cartography retains additional bends.

correspondence.component_scope: Intermediate south-turning reach
correspondence.finding: The next selected fragment follows the mapped border river as it turns southeast.

correspondence.component_scope: Longer southeastward lower corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected reach corresponds to the continuous southeastward meandering river shown in the hydraulic-study map.

correspondence.component_scope: Short lower bend
correspondence.finding: The short fragment occupies the connected lower bend between the southeastward approach and eastward lowland reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower arc and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The lower river continues east, turns north through the Sixaola–Palma corridor, then bends toward the coast.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected terminal reach
correspondence.finding: The final fragment corresponds to the coastal Sixaola outlet reach. Exact shoreline and active mouth position are not certified.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and small water body near Lajes
correspondence.finding: The original shows Rio Lajes running north toward Lajes and a small water body just south of the town, in the selected western approach. It does not provide sufficient continuous geographic detail to establish the chosen opening, its passage through that mapped impoundment and the upper receiving join. The water body is not given a name from proximity or an uninspected source.

correspondence.component_scope: Lajes to Pedra Preta–Jardim de Angicos upper continuation
correspondence.finding: The regional map depicts intermittent upper drainage northeast and east from the Lajes setting, south of Pedra Preta and through Jardim de Angicos toward the named Ceará-Mirim. The selected broad course is consistent with that drainage. This does not close the unresolved headward connection or authorize assigning every upper part the Ceará-Mirim label.

correspondence.component_scope: Named central trunk south of João Câmara
correspondence.finding: The river is directly labelled Rio Ceará-Mirim downstream of the RN-023/Jardim de Angicos setting and follows the selected eastward corridor south of João Câmara. Riacho da Onça and Riacho do Juá enter as side drainage; their names are not applied to the selected receiving trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Poço Branco impoundment and approach to Taipu
correspondence.finding: The original map shows a larger water body immediately south of Poço Branco in the river valley, with the eastward receiving river continuing toward Taipu. The catalog abstract independently identifies the Barragem de Poço Branco as a major surface-water feature of this study area. Neither inspected source establishes the selected route's actual impoundment through-link and both adjoining river connections. No dam-operation, present inundation or precise bank claim is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Taipu and eastward valley
correspondence.finding: The original river continues through the Taipu setting and bends east/northeast into the repeatedly named lower Ceará-Mirim valley. The upper reservoir connection remains a separate material gap and is not inferred from the common river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Ceará-Mirim valley and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The original directly labels the trunk north of Ceará-Mirim town and depicts the selected eastward lower valley, with branching channels and subsequent convergence toward the southeastern coastal exit. Rio do Mudo and Rio Guairu, together with the separate water body at Extremoz, lie south of this corridor and are not selected-route names. No individual managed channel or every small branch is separately named.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual final selected southeastward reach and Atlantic ending
correspondence.finding: The original maps a continuous lower river turning southeast through the Extremoz coastal setting and reaching the Atlantic at the selected terminal setting. It is north of the separate Extremoz lake outlet and north of Natal/Potengi. The inspected survey prose corroborates an Extremoz ocean destination. This is regional mouth correspondence, not a current tidal-channel or exact shoreline determination.
